title: Choose the visual world for AiPoker
question: The roll assigned Card-Room Print. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Card-Room Print
options.lineage: classic playing-card printing: engraved card backs, court-card inks, tuck-box index type
options.thesis: The whole table printed like a premium deck: two inks, engraved line, index typography.
materials: engraved guilloche line on deep baize
ivory card stock for cards and plates only
court-card vermilion as the single loud ink
options.viewport: Ink-navy room, deep green baize oval with a faint engraved rosette; the pot sits inside a card-back medallion at center; ivory seat plates with condensed index numerals; action bar bottom-right.
options.risk: Engraving can tip into casino kitsch if the line work is louder than the data.

raised.raise: All neutrals come from one tinted ink ramp (11 steps), no ad-hoc greys.
A strict seat state vocabulary: to-act, waiting, folded, all-in, winner, each exactly one treatment.
The acting seat lifts while the rest of the ring dims one step.
Bets in the hand log carry a bar sized to bet / pot, so sizing reads without arithmetic.
Every number right-aligned tabular; pot visibly equals the sum of the bets.
One display face repeated at fixed scale steps for every number on the table.

options.label: Broadcast Feature Table
options.lineage: televised poker graphics: hole-card cam lower thirds, live equity percentages
options.thesis: Play your session as if it were the featured table on a poker broadcast.
options.viewport: Near-black stage, green felt; each seat is a broadcast lower-third with name, stack, and a live hand-strength strip; coach equity shown like TV win percentages.
options.risk: Familiar: most modern poker clients borrow this look, and live equity on opponents would leak information, so it must show only hero equity until showdown.

options.label: Bitmap Type Specimen
options.thesis: Pixel display type at poster scale.
options.viewport: Stacks and pot in coarse pixel numerals.
options.case: Fuses poorly: learners do not identify with type specimens; pixel numerals slow reading.
options.kept: One display face repeated at fixed scale steps.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Time read upward on a center staff.
options.viewport: Hand history as a vertical score.
options.risk: Turns the table into a diagram.
options.case: Only the hand log benefits; the table loses clarity.
options.kept: Bet bars sized to bet / pot in the log.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Opponents as poster tiles that expand on focus.
options.viewport: Lobby as rows of bot opponents.
options.risk: No table metaphor; needs artwork we do not have.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.viewport: Hand log inked like a tracklist.
options.case: Fuses poorly with a timed decision screen.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Panels as hued tab sections with acetate leaves.
options.viewport: Side panel tabs in section hues.
options.risk: Too many hues compete with suit colors.

options.label: Darkroom Zone Sheets
options.thesis: An 11-step tonal ramp with hatch density as load.
options.risk: Monochrome felt kills suit and state color.

canonCard.label: PokerNow, played straight
canonCard.thesis: The flat online-poker standard, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Charcoal page, flat green oval, white plates, yellow bets, action bar bottom-right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from PokerNow by design; this is roughly what exists today.
